title: Sauptika: the night massacre
hook: a mother sits down and refuses to eat until she sees the jewel from her sons' killer's head
carry: a jewel carried home to a grieving mother

segments.voice: Your line: a vengeance that reaches everyone except its target. Yesterday the camp was struck in its sleep, Duryodhana died hearing of it, and the Pandavas weren't there. Who else did your anger nearly reach? Day eight hundred fifty-four.

Morning. Dhrishtadyumna's charioteer, one of the few who got away, brings the news to Yudhishthira, and the king falls to the ground. Then Draupadi comes. Her brother is dead. Her five sons are dead. She sits down in front of her husbands and says she'll take no food until Ashvatthama pays for this. And she names what she wants. Ashvatthama was born with a jewel on his head. She wants to see it brought back, and worn by Yudhishthira. Today, the end of the night book, and what happens to that jewel.
screen: `THE NEWS AT DAWN.` → `DRAUPADI SITS DOWN.` → `SHE ASKS FOR THE JEWEL.`

segments.voice: Bhima rides out at once. Krishna warns the others that Bhima is in danger: Drona once taught his son a weapon called Brahmashira, terrible enough to burn the worlds, and Ashvatthama is reckless enough to use it. So Krishna, Arjuna and Yudhishthira follow. They find Ashvatthama on the bank of the Ganga, sitting among sages with the sage Vyasa. When he sees them, he picks up a blade of grass, charges it as that weapon, and lets it go. Arjuna answers with the same weapon. Two fires rise to meet each other. And then two sages, Narada and Vyasa, step between the weapons to save the world. Arjuna, who has kept his vows, can call his weapon back, and he does. Ashvatthama can't. So he turns his toward the wombs of the Pandava women. Krishna answers that Uttara's child, the unborn son of Abhimanyu, will live, because Krishna himself will revive him. Then Krishna curses Ashvatthama: to wander the earth alone, sick, shunned, for a very long time. Ashvatthama gives up the jewel. They carry it back to Draupadi, and she hands it to Yudhishthira, and he wears it. This week opened in the shadow of a blow on a holy plain, and it closes with a jewel on a king's head. The night book ends with a grieving mother's demand met, and the next generation saved by one promise.
screen: `THE WEAPON IN A BLADE OF GRASS` · `TWO SAGES STEP BETWEEN` · `KRISHNA'S CURSE` · then, large: `THE JEWEL FOR DRAUPADI`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your breath find its own pace. Bring to mind a time someone stepped between two angry people, or between you and something you were about to do. Breathe in, and remember how it felt to be stopped. Breathe out, and let a little thanks rise for the one who stepped in. If you pray, you can remember them in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Sauptika. The night book ends by the Ganga: two weapons, two sages between them, a curse, and a jewel carried home to a grieving mother.
Your line: a jewel carried home to a grieving mother. Today, if you see two people heating up, try one calm word between them. Tomorrow, the book of the women: Stri. Day eight hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Ashvatthama's wandering under Krishna's curse is told in retellings of the epic, and some Hindus tell stories of him still wandering the earth.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. your weapon and Ashvatthama's are blazing toward each other, and two sages have stepped between them. what do you do?
options: let your weapon finish the fight.
turn your weapon toward Ashvatthama alone.
fork.reveal: Arjuna calls his weapon back; Ashvatthama can't, and turns his toward the unborn.

original.note: jewel: the gem on Ashvatthama's head that Draupadi asks for.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas killed Ashvatthama for the night attack.
what it means: he lost his jewel and was cursed to wander, and Draupadi's demand was met.
what a scholar hears: Krishna's promise to revive Uttara's child is how the line of the Pandavas goes on, so the night book ends looking forward.

notes: Audit pass: Brahmashira warning, the blade of grass, Narada and Vyasa, the turn toward the wombs, Krishna's promise for Uttara's child, the curse and the jewel checked; no change needed.
All paraphrase. Krishna's curse in Ganguli names a specific span of years; it is left out on purpose ('a very long time').
Confirm: Dhrishtadyumna's charioteer brings the news; Draupadi's vow to fast; the jewel 'born with' Ashvatthama; Yudhishthira wears it at Draupadi's wish.
Confirm Krishna, Arjuna and Yudhishthira follow Bhima; Ashvatthama is found with Vyasa and other sages on the Ganga; the weapon charged into a blade of grass.
Confirm Narada and Vyasa stand between the weapons and the reason Arjuna can withdraw his (vows/brahmacharya) while Ashvatthama cannot.
